content.title: Salvador (TV Series 2026) ⭐ 6.4 | Crime, Drama, Mystery
content.text: Episodes8Videos1Featured reviewsUncomfortable & unflinching, yet still engrossing...This is quite an uncomfortable viewing, albeit a surprisingly very engrossing one too. We have a redemption arc of an estranged father, Salvador, who finds that his grown up daughter is involved with some far-right Nazi sympathising hooligans in their home city of Madrid. He finds himself involved to find what went wrong and then is involved in police investigations as all goes wrong, with a journey of self-discovery in this turbulent world.The real crux of the show is the emotional heart, led by Luis Tosar as Salvador, in a very visceral performance. The rest of the ensemble are themselves very good in a tough unflinching storyline that takes us across the stratosphere of lives in Madrid.To give the show credit, they avoided a number of cliches, but that is partly how it becomes uncomfortable. As much as the far-right are shown to be the odious manipulative bunch they are, the storyline also delves into it a bit deeper to try to explain how otherwise "good" people end up in their clutches. Salvador is the father who is similarly trying to understand how his daughter has fallen in with that lot, but in some ways becomes himself a touch endeared by certain aspects of them.I don't want to give anything away. It does have some faults, and some might fairly argue that the far-right are given too easy a ride in this series, but it is still clearly an anti-Nazi storyline. I think it does struggle to put forward what it wants, but thankfully not in a preachy manner. Maybe towards the end it loses its way but still that won't deter from what was attempted.I'd argue it's very watchable. Not long, just six episodes. Give it a shot but as said, it's uncomfortable and not for everyone.Underrated Series on Contemporary Social IssuesSalvador, a Netflix series brimming with urgent social themes, deserves far more attention. It plunges into the worlds of ultranationalists, neo-Nazis, public violence, hooligans, incels, and the surge of extreme right-wing movements across Europe. Through the intertwined stories of a father consumed by revenge after losing his daughter and a young woman fighting for custody of her child, the show exposes the dark alliances between corrupt politicians, complicit law enforcers, and the wealthy who profit from chaos. Set against the backdrop of contemporary Spain, Salvador offers a sharp, balanced critique of European society. While it may not be a masterpiece, the conversations it sparks and the bold stance it takes make it well worth your time.Gripping, different and entertaining!I really enjoyed the series, and I think it's underrated. It's quite addictive and goes by quickly.The series gets off to a strong start. The first episode features one intense scene after another, supplemented by heavy action.The plot explores themes of ideological extremism, familial neglect, and the moral boundaries of a father seeking redemption.It's refreshing to see a doctor as the antihero in an action drama with thriller elements, instead of the usual detective or police officer. The only negative is that Salvador Aguirre is rather a confusingly written character full of contradictions, and that makes it quite difficult to identify with him.I personally loved the dinner episode, it's very exciting.The series is worthwhile from beginning to end and deals with a very current topic; if you like action and some good dialogues, don't miss it!Underrated, Yet, Very Actual!I don't really know what some of the reviews here mean with leaving the show in Spanish since the original language of the show is in Spanish but okay. On with the review.I'm not going to delve deep in the plot but Netflix's Salvador follows the story of a father who sees himself in the midst of a radical group that started in football clubs and follow on the footsteps of English hooligans.This show mirrors the football scene in many European nations, Including my own Portugal.On the small break I took binging this show a major battle broke out between 2 football club Ultras group. 124 people were detained for mass chaos with very light torches, baseball bats, belts and fireworks being used. After a brief interrogation most were already released. So yeah the show is 100% spot on.fast start and downhill all the way to endVery promising first episode with opposing terrorist groups battling against each other...leading character's daughter is murdered and after setting the premise the remaining 7 episodes is a mish mash of horrible police work and silly portrayals of each side of the fight....acting is over the top and the dialogue is horrible..perhaps they should have left it in Spanish and not butchered the English translation...typical Netflix junk.More like thisRelated interestsEverything New on Netflix in FebruaryEverything New on Netflix in February"The Night Agent" and "The Lincoln Lawyer" return this month.
